title: Body Fluids and Circulation
seo_title: Body Fluids and Circulation Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 15)
standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation
standard_text: Composition of blood, blood groups, coagulation of blood; composition of lymph and its function; human circulatory system – structure of human heart and blood vessels; cardiac cycle, cardiac output, ECG; double circulation; regulation of cardiac activity; disorders of circulatory system – hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina pectoris, heart failure.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 15 Body Fluids and Circulation: blood cells, plasma, blood groups, clotting, lymph, the heart, cardiac cycle, cardiac output, ECG, double circulation and disorders. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume.
key_sub: Blood flows twice through the heart in one circuit.
body_html:
How to think about it

Blood is plasma (55%) with red cells, white cells and platelets. ABO groups depend on antigens A and B on red cells; Rh mismatch can cause erythroblastosis foetalis. Clotting needs platelets, Ca²⁺ and fibrinogen turning into fibrin.

The human heart has four chambers; the SA node starts each beat, passed on by the AV node and bundle of His. At rest the heart beats about 72 times a minute with a stroke volume of about 70 mL, so cardiac output is about 5 L/min. The ECG shows P (atria), QRS (ventricles) and T waves.

Example

72 beats × 70 mL?

HR × SV

Answer: 5040 mL/min

Example

Universal recipient?

no antibodies

Answer: AB

Common mistakes

  • Calling AB the universal donor.
  • Thinking the P-wave is ventricular.
  • Mixing up the SA and AV nodes.

faq.a: The volume of blood each ventricle pumps per minute: heart rate × stroke volume, about 5 litres at rest.

faq.q: Why is group O a universal donor?
faq.a: Its red cells carry no A or B antigens, so they are not clumped by anti-A or anti-B antibodies.

items.q: Which of these is a plasma protein?
items.e: “Fibrinogen” is a plasma protein.

items.q: What is lymph?
c: tissue fluid in lymph vessels, containing lymphocytes
items.e: It returns fluid to the blood.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a plasma protein?
items.e: “Neutrophil” is not a plasma protein; the other three are.

items.q: What is the role of platelets?
c: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic
releasing factors that help blood clot
the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
items.e: Platelets: releasing factors that help blood clot.

items.q: Which of these is an agranulocyte?
items.e: “Monocyte” is an agranulocyte.

items.q: Which is the hepatic portal system?
c: veins that carry blood from the intestine to the liver before it returns to the heart
items.e: The liver processes absorbed food.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a granulocyte?
items.e: “Globulin” is not a granulocyte; the other three are.

items.q: What does the P-wave of an ECG show?
items.e: QRS shows ventricular depolarisation; T shows ventricular repolarisation.

items.q: What is the role of neutrophils?
c: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic
passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles
items.e: Neutrophils: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic.

items.q: What is the role of AV node?
c: B and T cells of the immune response
passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles
releasing factors that help blood clot
items.e: AV node: passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles.

items.q: What is the role of SA node?
c: B and T cells of the immune response
the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
items.e: SA node: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat.

items.q: What is the role of eosinophils?
c: passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles
the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
items.e: Eosinophils: resisting infections and allergic reactions.

items.q: Which blood group is the universal donor?
items.e: Its cells carry no A or B antigen.

items.q: Which of these is an agranulocyte?
items.e: “Lymphocyte” is an agranulocyte.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for B and T cells of the immune response?
items.e: Lymphocytes: B and T cells of the immune response.

items.q: What is the role of fibrinogen?
c: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic
items.e: Fibrinogen: forming fibrin threads in clotting.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for forming fibrin threads in clotting?
items.e: Fibrinogen: forming fibrin threads in clotting.

items.q: Which condition can occur when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive baby for the second time?
items.e: Her anti-Rh antibodies destroy the baby's red cells.

items.q: How many litres of blood does a healthy adult have?
items.e: Plasma is about 55% of it.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for resisting infections and allergic reactions?
items.e: Eosinophils: resisting infections and allergic reactions.

items.q: Which antigen is on the red blood cells of a person with blood group B?
items.e: Blood group B: antigen B on the red cells, anti-A in the plasma.

items.q: Which antigen is on the red blood cells of a person with blood group AB?
items.e: Blood group AB: antigens A and B on the red cells, no antibodies in the plasma.

items.q: What is atherosclerosis (coronary artery disease)?
c: narrowing of the arteries by deposits of calcium, fat and cholesterol
items.e: It can lead to a heart attack.

items.q: Which antibodies are in the plasma of blood group B?
items.e: Blood group B has anti-A in the plasma.

items.q: Which antibodies are in the plasma of blood group O?
items.e: Blood group O has anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: What is the life span of a red blood cell?
items.e: They are destroyed in the spleen.

items.q: Which antibodies are in the plasma of blood group A?
items.e: Blood group A has anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Which blood group has anti-A in its plasma?
items.e: Blood group B has anti-A in the plasma.

items.q: Cardiac output is 3.84 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 60 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 3,840 ÷ 60 = 64 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Which blood group has no antigens on its red blood cells?
items.e: Blood group O: no antigens on the red cells, anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: What is the normal blood pressure of a healthy adult?
items.e: Systolic over diastolic.

items.q: Which blood group has antigens A and B on its red blood cells?
items.e: Blood group AB: antigens A and B on the red cells, no antibodies in the plasma.

items.q: Which blood group has antigen A on its red blood cells?
items.e: Blood group A: antigen A on the red cells, anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Pulmonary ventilation is 10 L min⁻¹ at 20 breaths per minute. Calculate the tidal volume.
items.e: Tidal volume = ventilation ÷ breathing rate = 0.5 L.

items.q: Which type of circulation do fishes have?
items.e: Blood passes through the heart once per circuit.

items.q: Which blood group has anti-A and anti-B in its plasma?

items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 4,200 mL min⁻¹ = 4.2 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat?

items.q: What is angina pectoris?
c: acute chest pain when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle
items.e: It is a warning sign of heart disease.

items.q: Cardiac output is 6.6 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 60 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
What is the role of basophils?
c: passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles
items.e: Basophils: secreting histamine, serotonin and heparin.

items.q: Which sound of the heart is 'lub'?
c: the closing of the semilunar valves
the closing of the tricuspid and bicuspid (AV) valves
items.e: 'Dub' is the closing of the semilunar valves.

items.q: How many heartbeats does a healthy adult have each minute at rest?
items.e: It is set by the SA node.

items.q: Cardiac output is 7.2 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 80 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
What is the role of bundle of His?
c: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum
releasing factors that help blood clot
items.e: Bundle of His: carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum.
